name: Copy on write
problem: Most consumers read data, so eagerly copying every borrowed value wastes work, but one consumer may need an independent update.

origin.summary: Historical priority, inventor and first adoption remain unresolved. The cited primary documentation establishes the described mechanism, not its invention.

mechanism: A wrapper retains borrowed/shared storage for reads and creates owned storage when mutation requires it. Exact sharing and uniqueness tests depend on the representation.
solutionFamily: Lazy ownership conversion versus eager clone
costs: First write can allocate and copy.
Large writes can cause latency spikes hidden by cheap reads.
transferRule: Track the transition from borrowed/shared to owned at the mutation boundary.
confidence: MEDIUM: mechanism anchored to primary documentation; historical attribution and unknown language cells unresolved; traces are editorial reasoning examples.
examples: Rust Cow<str> starts Borrowed('cat'); reading makes no owned String. to_mut().push('s') creates owned 'cats'; the original borrowed text stays 'cat'.
counterexamples: Copy on write is not a promise that every write is cheap or that nested reference objects are isolated.

assessment.prompt: An image editor keeps ten previews and changes one. Explain when copy cost is paid and what to measure.
rubric: Measure copied size and repeated write behavior.
